chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man is able to afford what he uses to perform Hajj, then he spends it, and he has no excuse that God excuses him for, then he has left a pillar from the pillars of Islam. If he is wealthy and an illness or confinement or a matter that excuses him before God stands between him and Hajj, then it is upon him to send someone else to perform Hajj on his behalf from his wealth, a person who has no wealth."
And he said, "The Hajj of Islam (the obligatory Hajj) is paid for on behalf of the man from all of his wealth."

key_terms.صَرُورَةً: A substitute/person performing Hajj on behalf of another

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a wealthy Muslim dies without performing the obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that neglecting Hajj without a valid excuse constitutes abandoning a fundamental pillar of Islam, while excused delays (like illness) allow for performance from the estate. It establishes the principle that Hajj al-Islam is fulfilled from the deceased's entire wealth, prioritizing this religious debt over other bequests, a ruling central to Shia jurisprudence regarding inheritance and religious obligations.
